hints: Start by drawing the dot-and-cross picture for Cl-N=O and count what is around nitrogen, bonds plus any lone pairs.
Remember a double bond N=O is one sigma plus one pi, while a single bond Cl-N is just one sigma, so add them up carefully.
Use the total number of electron domains on nitrogen to predict its shape and its hybridisation type.
walkthrough:
**Draw the structure around nitrogen**

Think of nitrosyl chloride as $\text{Cl}-\text{N}=\text{O}$ with a lone pair left on nitrogen. That gives nitrogen two bonding domains and one lone pair.

Count domains: $$2 \text{ bonding domains} + 1 \text{ lone pair} = 3 \text{ electron domains}$$

**Count sigma and pi bonds**

A single bond is always one sigma bond. A double bond is one sigma plus one pi.

So here: $$\text{Cl}-\text{N (single)} = 1\sigma$$ $$\text{N}=\text{O (double)} = 1\sigma + 1\pi$$ Total $= 2\sigma + 1\pi$.

**Predict shape and polarity**

Three electron domains gives trigonal planar electron geometry, but with one lone pair the molecular shape is bent, not linear. A bent molecule with different atoms ($\text{Cl}$ and $\text{O}$) and polar bonds cannot cancel dipoles, so it is polar.

**Assign hybridisation of nitrogen**

The rule is simple: 2 domains = sp, 3 domains = $\text{sp}^2$, 4 domains = $\text{sp}^3$. Since nitrogen has 3 domains here, it is $\text{sp}^2$ hybridised, with one p orbital left to form the pi bond to oxygen.

options.A: Incorrect. The molecule has two sigma bonds (Cl-N and one part of N=O) and only one pi bond (the second part of N=O). Students who pick this often miscount the double bond as two pi bonds.
options.B: Incorrect. Cl-N=O is bent and contains polar Cl-N and N=O bonds with different electronegativities. The dipoles do not cancel, so the molecule is polar.
options.C: Incorrect. Nitrogen has a lone pair as well as two bonds, so repulsion bends the molecule. It is angular or bent, with a bond angle around 113 degrees, not 180 degrees.
options.D: Correct. Nitrogen has 3 electron domains (one Cl-N bond, one N=O bond domain, one lone pair). Three domains corresponds to sp2 hybridisation, leaving one unhybridised p orbital for the pi bond to oxygen.
